\chapter{Measurement protocols of the engine}\label{t2ann:protocoles}

\begin{origine}
\textbf{Where we start.} The measurement rules of Volume~I (its appendix A, \enquote{Measurement protocols}): the provenance label of every number, the witness and its break, the threshold declared beforehand, ABBA series and the decision rule, the second path, power and the shared machine, the quality judge. They all hold here, as they are.
\textbf{What this appendix establishes.} What construction added to them: an end criterion for every step of every lot, with its witness, its break and the derivation of its threshold; the proof that a palindrome cancels a linear drift; the lock of the card; the time of the commit as the proof that a threshold precedes its pass; the protocol of the trial and that of the round of corrections, block by block.
\textbf{What remains.} Two protocols the machine has not yet allowed: a single palindromic series containing both guarded troncons and the best baseline, and a baseline beyond 16 threads and with \texttt{--mlock} (\cref{ch:t2-discussion}).
\end{origine}

\section{What is inherited from Volume~I}\label{t2ann:sec:herite}

Every number carries its provenance (\mes, \calc, \litt). Every measurement has its witness, a case whose answer is known in advance, and every new witness must be able to fail: its condition is forced to false, the run is repeated, the instrument is checked to fall, then restored. A threshold derives from a named measured quantity, and is declared before the run. A cost is never founded on a single pass. Every published number we depend on is redone by an independent path. Only passes on mains power are reference throughputs. The decision rule is that of study 06, \S\,7.5, recalled in \cref{t2res-def:reel}: a configuration $B$ really differs from $A$ if
\begin{equation}\label{t2ann:eq:regle}
\Bigl|\frac{\bar X_B}{\bar X_A} - 1\Bigr| \;>\; 2\,\max(\beta_A, \beta_B) + 3\,\%,
\qquad \beta = \frac{|X_1 - X_2|}{\bar X},
\end{equation}
where $\beta$ is the noise of a configuration, the gap between its two passes of one palindrome relative to their mean.

\section{The end criteria of each step}\label{t2ann:sec:etapes}

The architecture wrote, before the first line of code, what would make each step hold (\fichier{decisions/ARCHITECTURE.md}, \S\,6.5). \Cref{t2ann:tab:etapes} restates them, with the chapter where each is judged. The factor $0.8$ recurs everywhere; it is not a margin chosen by guesswork: it is $1 - 2 \times 10\,\%$, where $10\,\%$ is the noise measured in Volume~I of a 4\,MiB read at queue depth 4 (study 01). A throughput measured above $0.8$ times its reference therefore cannot be declared slower than it through the noise of the two measurements alone.

\paragraph{The thresholds, step by step.} Each is redone from named numbers \calc:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{E0\,(b)}: the host $\to$ card DMA measured in Volume~I is 12.2\,GB/s; minus its 10\,\% noise, $12.2 \times 0.9 = 10.98 \approx 11.0$\,GB/s.
\item \textbf{E0\,(c)}: in Volume~I's calibrated LRU scenario, the disk takes 157\,ms per token of the 120b; a synchronisation costing at most a tenth of it, $15.7$\,ms, does not change the slowest stage.
\item \textbf{E2}: 2.58\,GB/s is the disk throughput for 4\,MiB reads measured in Volume~I (study 01); served as chunks compressed at rate $r$, these bytes are worth $2.58\,r$\,GB/s of decoded experts; the factor $0.8$ covers the noise.
\item \textbf{K1}: $0.8 \times 41.6 = 33.28$\,GB/s, where 41.6\,GB/s was the throughput published by study 03 for the path K1 replaces. That number was itself composed under Vulkan; redone under CUDA it is 45.8\,GB/s, and the corrected threshold $0.8 \times 45.8 = 36.6$\,GB/s. The kernels chapter strikes out the first and judges against both (\cref{sec:t2n-decodeur}).
\item \textbf{K2}: $0.8 \times 209.4 = 167.5$\,GB/s, where 209.4\,GB/s is study 03's raw MXFP4 GEMV.
\item \textbf{C5}: $0.8$ times the serial floor $t_{\text{série}}$ recomputed \emph{in the same session}, with the $h$ counted by the engine and the throughputs the \texttt{troncons disque} pass has just measured (\cref{t2res-sec:vitesse}).
\item \textbf{C7}: 1.9\,GB is the peak RAM of mode A0 published by study 07, which the minimal window (0.64\,GB) had to beat; 0.5\,MB is the directory, the only term believed to grow with the model (finding M4 of the trial found others, \cref{t2arch:sec:fenetre}).
\item \textbf{C10}: $8{,}188 - 909 = 7{,}279$\,MiB, the card's memory minus the 909\,MiB that the display and applications held in it at the reading of 15 October at 10:15, card free (\fichier{mesures/REPRISE-gpt-oss.md}).
\end{itemize}

\section{A threshold precedes its pass: the time of the commit is proof}\label{t2ann:sec:heure}

A threshold declared \enquote{beforehand} proves nothing if nothing dates the declaration. Every block of thresholds is therefore committed \emph{before} the first pass it judges, and it is the time of the commit, not the one written in the text, that is proof. \Cref{t2ann:tab:seuils} gives, for every threshold file, the commit that created it and the number of commits that touched it afterwards (blocks added, each before its pass; never a threshold changed after its own).

\section{ABBA series and palindromes}\label{t2ann:sec:palindromes}

The sessions of this volume are not A~B pairs but \emph{palindromes}: the order of the passes reads the same both ways. The trial's session begins with D120 T120 L120 L120t10 L120t10 L120 T120 D120 (troncons disque, troncons, llama.cpp with 6 then 10 threads); the swept baseline of the round, after a discarded warm-up pass, with t6 t10 t12 t16 m m t16 t12 t10 t6 (\fichier{mesures/moteur/O/corrections/seuils-declares.md}, block 6). The reason is a lemma.

\begin{lemme}[A palindrome cancels a linear drift]\label{t2ann:lem:palindrome}
Let a session have $n$ passes at times $1, \dots, n$, and $s_i$ the configuration of pass $i$, with $s_i = s_{n+1-i}$ for all $i$. Assume pass $i$ measures $X_i = \mu_{s_i} + a + b\,i + \varepsilon_i$, where $\mu_c$ is the true value of configuration $c$, $a + b\,i$ a linear drift of the machine (warm-up, foreign load rising or falling) and $\varepsilon_i$ a zero-mean noise. Then, for two configurations $c$ and $c'$, the expectation of $\bar X_c - \bar X_{c'}$ is exactly $\mu_c - \mu_{c'}$: the drift vanishes, whatever $a$ and $b$.
\end{lemme}
\begin{proof}
Let $I_c = \{\, i : s_i = c \,\}$, of cardinality $n_c$. Since $s_i = s_{n+1-i}$, the map $i \mapsto n+1-i$ sends $I_c$ into itself; it is an involution, hence a bijection of $I_c$. Then
\[
\sum_{i \in I_c} i \;=\; \sum_{i \in I_c} (n+1-i) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{1}{n_c}\sum_{i \in I_c} i \;=\; \frac{n+1}{2}.
\]
The expectation of $\bar X_c = \frac{1}{n_c}\sum_{i\in I_c} X_i$ is therefore $\mu_c + a + b\,\frac{n+1}{2}$. The drift term, $a + b\,(n+1)/2$, is the same for all configurations, and cancels in the difference.
\end{proof}

\begin{remarque}
The lemma holds only for a linear drift: a curved drift (a disk that cools quickly, then slowly) leaves a second-order term. It holds only for the part of the session that is a palindrome: the last four passes of the trial (T20 T20 T120tiede1 T120) do not form a palindrome with the rest, and the ratio comparing them to it is protected only by rule~\eqref{t2ann:eq:regle}. The noise $\beta$ of a configuration measures the gap between two \emph{symmetric} passes: it contains the drift between them, so the rule is stricter when the machine drifts. This is intended.
\end{remarque}

The rule applies to the means of each configuration, never to a single pass. A warm-up pass is discarded when it precedes the series. Finding m1 of the trial gives the reason in numbers: the first \texttt{troncons disque} pass of its session read at 0.725\,GB/s (90th percentile: 172\,ms per read), the second at 1.822\,GB/s, and the median of the two moved the threshold of C5 by 25\,\% (1.12 instead of 1.47 tokens/s; C5 held in both cases) \mes~(\fichier{mesures/epreuve-J1.md}, m1). The round of corrections has since discarded a warm-up D pass before its series (block 3); the general rule awaits the arbiter's decision (\cref{ch:t2-epreuve}).

\section{The lock of the card and the shared machine}\label{t2ann:sec:verrou}

The card is a single resource, and other agents were working on the machine. Before any session that measures it, the driver script waits until the file \fichier{~/dev/verrou-carte.txt} is absent or older than two hours, then writes it in its own name (lot, date, tool, process number) and gives it back at the end (\fichier{mesures/moteur/O/pilote_o4.py}, and the driver scripts of lots E and K). Before \emph{every} pass it reads and logs the power state (\texttt{Win32\_Battery.BatteryStatus}, 2: mains), the live \texttt{llama-*} processes and the occupied VRAM; it stops if the machine is not on mains. The lock of the round of corrections was taken at 06:41, renewed at 07:21, 08:13 and 09:14, and given back at 10:06 (\fichier{moteur/REPRISE-O.md}); the trial's, taken at 02:26 and given back at 04:44 (\cref{t2e-sec:protocole}).

The lock protects the card, not the rest. Foreign processor and disk load is recorded and left, never killed: no process one did not start is killed (SOCLE). \enquote{Best} throughputs therefore remain lower bounds of the idle machine, as in Volume~I. The tools of lot F, which do not need the card, run at \enquote{below normal} priority (\fichier{mesures/moteur/F/lancer.ps1}), and builds each go to their own target, with four jobs (\texttt{-j 4}), because five lots were compiling at once.

Before correcting a finding, lot O replayed it on a frozen copy of the earlier program (commit \texttt{7b288a6}); the witness had to fall on the old one and hold on the new one (\cref{t2e-sec:ronde}).

\section{The independent trial}\label{t2ann:sec:epreuve}

The protocol is written in \S\,8 of the architecture, before any construction, and followed in \cref{ch:t2-epreuve}. The judge wrote neither the specification nor the code; he works from a clean clone (commit \texttt{527dff5}), on mains, card free, and reads only the specification, the code and the logs. His seven gestures: (1) a decoder written from \S\,4 alone, on 20 chunks drawn at random (seed published); (2) every break replayed; (3) C3, C4, C5, C7, C8, C10 redone in ABBA series with his own commands, judged by rule~\eqref{t2ann:eq:regle}; (4) the baseline rerun, and another configuration of his choice; (5) the window: 1\,GiB of warm cache must appear in the peak memory, between 0.9 and 1.1 times; (6) the text read; (7) the verdict, with his own \enquote{What could be wrong} section. His thresholds are in \fichier{mesures/moteur/epreuve-J1/seuils-declares.md}, committed before his first pass (\cref{t2ann:tab:seuils}).

\section{Reproducing the builds}\label{t2ann:sec:construction}

A published number is reproducible only if the program that produced it rebuilds. Three rules ensure it. \emph{One target per lot and per judge}: each build writes to its own output folder, outside the repository (\fichier{mesures/moteur/E/construire.bat}, \fichier{mesures/moteur/epreuve-J1/construire.bat}), so that two lots do not overwrite each other. \emph{The judge starts from a clean clone}, at a named commit (\texttt{527dff5}, built in 21\,s). \emph{The machine's recipe is tested by a witness}: the trial found that the SOCLE's recipe (\texttt{vcvars64.bat} first) broke the build of the kernels (finding m2); since the correction, block 2 of the round requires that building with and without it gives the same kernel image to the byte (\fichier{mesures/moteur/O/corrections/construire-avec-vcvars.bat}).

\begin{faux}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The reference noise of 10\,\%} comes from a Volume~I measurement (a 4\,MiB read at queue depth 4); the chunks of the 120b, about 12\,MB each, are read in a single request each. The factor $0.8$ inherits it without having been remeasured for that length; \cref{ch:t2-chemin} shows that the length changes the regime of the disk.
\item \textbf{The palindrome lemma assumes a linear drift.} The machine's encrypted disk varies from 1.51 to 1.95\,GB/s from one pass to the next within a single session (\cref{t2res-sec:garde}): this is not a drift, it is a dispersion, which the palindrome does not remove and which only the rule covers.
\item \textbf{The lock is a convention, not a mechanism of the system}: a program that does not read it can take the card. The driver scripts read the VRAM before every pass to see it, but a brief use between two readings would go unnoticed.
\item \textbf{C6 is judged across two sessions} (guarded troncons in the round's session, the baseline in the next); the lemma does not protect a comparison between sessions. The single series remains to be done (\cref{ch:t2-discussion}).
\end{itemize}
\end{faux}
